title: Multi-region degradation interim brief and remediation timeline
content:
Purpose
This is a customer-facing draft covering the interim public status updates and a concise remediation timeline for the multi-region inference degradation that began 2027-01-09 22:14 UTC. Goal: give customers a clear, non-technical status page snippet plus a more detailed customer summary and commitments on next steps and compensations.

Executive summary (customer-facing)
On 2027-01-09 at ~22:14 UTC, Redwood experienced a performance degradation affecting inference latency and request failures for a subset of hosted API requests routed through our US-west and EU regions. Impact varied by customer and endpoint; the highest impact was observed for low-latency chat routes and long-context generation. We restored primary routing for most customers by 2027-01-10 03:47 UTC with staged rollbacks and targeted cache rebuilds. Residual elevated latency persisted in specific zones until 2027-01-11 10:20 UTC.

Short status page drafts (choose one, keep concise)
- Option A (short): Investigating — We are addressing increased latency and some failed requests in US-west and EU regions. Our engineers are rolling back a recent runtime change and restoring caches. We will post updates as available.
- Option B (update): Partial restoration — Primary routing restored for most customers. Some regions still show elevated latency while we complete cache reconciliation and increased capacity. No ongoing request failures expected for most endpoints.
- Option C (closure): Resolved — Service restored to normal performance. We completed a rollback and targeted cache rebuilds; monitoring continues.

Customer email / longer status (for high-touch accounts)
Hi — we want to share what happened and what we did to resolve it. At 22:14 UTC on Jan 9 a coordinated rollout of a serving-runtime kernel and cache replication optimization triggered unexpected cache-eviction patterns across a narrow set of nodes. The eviction pattern caused increased cold-starts for KV caches and, combined with a routing flap, amplified load on remaining nodes. This increased latency and produced intermittent 500/502 errors for affected routes.
What we did:
- Immediately paused the rollout and initiated a rollback to the previous runtime image. (Jan 9, 22:28 UTC)
- Rebalanced routing to unaffected zones and promoted fallback model variants that are CPU-optimized to reduce tail latency. (Jan 9–10)
- Triggered targeted KV cache rebuilds and rehydration for affected node pools. (Jan 10, 01:12–03:47 UTC)
- Increased temporary capacity and applied a conservative autoscaler profile to avoid aggressive eviction until we deliver a code fix.

Customer impact summary (concise)
- Affected customers: those on hosted API routes in US-west and EU regions using long-context or chat routes; Dedicated customers with pinned GPUs were largely unaffected unless using cross-region failover.
- Symptoms: increased token latency (median increase 2.8x), elevated 500/502 rates for a subset of mid-to-large requests, and some streaming interruptions (10–25% of streams for affected pools during peak).
- Duration: onset 2027-01-09 22:14 UTC; primary recovery for most customers by 2027-01-10 03:47 UTC; final stabilization for all zones by 2027-01-11 10:20 UTC.

Immediate remediation timeline (customer commitments)
- 0–24 hours (complete): customer-facing status updates, rollback completed, cache rehydration started, high-touch outreach to critical accounts.
- 24–72 hours (in progress): post-incident analysis and mitigations — we will publish a customer postmortem document with technical root cause and mitigations complete.
- 2–4 weeks: deploy a tested fix for the KV-cache eviction logic and update autoscaler tuning on staging and then prod.
- 30–60 days: full RCA verification, targeted load-testing with representative workloads, and an update to our runbook to prevent recurrence.

Proposed customer postmortem summary (one-paragraph version for external audiences)
On Jan 9, a runtime optimization rollout caused unanticipated interactions with our KV cache replication which produced a narrow cache-eviction bug on a small proportion of nodes. The resulting cold cache behavior plus a routing destabilization increased load on remaining nodes, raising latency and producing intermittent failures. We rolled back the change, rehydrated caches, and added capacity to stabilize traffic. Engineering is implementing a code fix to the eviction heuristic and improving rollout safeguards and autoscaler thresholds. We will provide a full technical postmortem and the timeline for code fixes within 72 hours.

Compensation / credits (template)
We recognize the impact to customers during this incident and will evaluate eligible accounts for pro-rated service credits per our SLA. Customers who experienced measurable availability loss (>= 10% of expected successful requests over an invoice period) will be flagged for account-level review. Customer Success will reach out to affected accounts with next steps.

Suggested CS Q&A (for support reps)
Q: Is my data affected?
A: No customer data loss has been detected. The issue impacted caching and routing behavior — not persisted customer data stores.
Q: Were private deployments affected?
A: No. Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments are not on the same rollout pipeline and were not affected.
Q: What can I do as a customer to reduce risk?
A: If you require lower tail latency, we recommend pinning to dedicated capacity or enabling regional pinning to avoid cross-region failovers while we finish the fix. For high-throughput chat workloads, consider enabling prefix caching and shorter max-context lengths until we ship the KV-cache fix.

Notes for internal reviewers (working thoughts)
- Need exact metric deltas from observability: median p50/p95/p99 token latency, error-rate curves across regions; attach graphs to final postmortem. (SRE action: SRE-613)
- Confirm list of affected customer accounts for CS outreach; reconcile with billing and incident classification. (Customer Success)
- Draft final external postmortem with sanitized technical detail — avoid internal IPs and hostnames.
- Check compensation thresholds with Finance/legal before committing credits broadly.

Open questions / items to resolve before publication
- Final root cause: eviction heuristic vs rollout ordering — both teams to confirm (Applied ML + Serving Runtime). Target: definitive root cause statement by 2027-01-12 17:00 UTC.
- Exact set of customers impacted and % of traffic per account that failed — authoritative list by 2027-01-12 12:00 UTC.
- Customer-facing timeline: agree wording for the closure notice (Option C above) and schedule for posting to status.redwood.ai.

Next steps (owners)
- Priya Nair (CS): finalize outreach emails to the top 25 affected accounts; send by 2027-01-12 09:00 UTC.
- Ethan Morales (SRE): attach p95/p99 graphs + error-rate heatmap to the postmortem draft by 2027-01-12 12:00 UTC.
- Sana Iqbal (Serving Runtime): confirm temporary mitigation patch and ETA for code fix, update by 2027-01-12 17:00 UTC.
- Jia Chen (Product): coordinate public postmortem publication and sign-off with legal.

Draft closure blurb (for status page and shorter email footer)
Resolved: We completed a rollback and targeted cache rehydration; normal performance has resumed across all regions. We are continuing post-incident monitoring and will publish a technical postmortem and corrective actions in the next 72 hours.

Appendix: suggested internal links to include in final release
- JIRA INFR-4822 (incident timeline)
- SRE dashboard: latency/error time series (attach)
- PR: serving-runtime PR #874 (rollback and temp mitigation)
- Confluence postmortem draft (internal)

-- end of draft --

Notes to self: keep external wording concise; avoid blame statements; focus on actions and customer impact; include an explicit timeline and next steps to reduce customer anxiety.
